<!-- pr-reviewer: fe3c8f6e029a44ddae4a4c5d0f93f95d58b60d9f -->
Needs changes before merge. This is a safety-tier review because the PR changes posted G-code.

The trial merge with upstream main `f85163b0ca948250fd6a51360d14754a282e0340` was clean. I read the current upstream `AGENTS.md`.

What looks good:

- The new modules state their provenance. The jet law has separate state from the torch law.
- The new NC goldens show the water and abrasive order. I checked every new golden line. No existing golden moved.
- The diff has no UI, dependency, workflow, script-directory, or build-script change.

Local results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: PASS. All 1,007 steps passed in 43.9 minutes. The CL change selects the batch plan.
- The gate built all selected crates locally with `--no-run`. All selected default suites passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- `waterjet_engine`: 12 passed. The CL library: 49 passed, including the three new jet tests.
- The UI library: 1,337 passed and 7 ignored. Pixel snapshots were not selected.
- The independent CLI checks reproduced the four behavior defects below. These checks gave no warning, except the machine-kind refusal in item 3.

Extra suites run:

I searched the Rust sources for the changed golden paths. These two suites read the new directories. I ran each again, in addition to the quick gate:

- `cargo test -j 16 -p camcraft-post --test waterjet_iso_post`: 7 passed.
- `cargo test -j 16 -p camcraft-post --test script_waterjet_iso`: 11 passed.

The importer rule does not apply. No importer or STEP fixture changed.

Independent mutation checks:

I ran two mutations from the PR's list. I changed one check at a time in the local review worktree.

| Mutation | Pin | Check removed | Check restored |
|---|---|---|---|
| Remove `travelOk()` | `waterjet_post_refuses_a_cut_outside_the_stated_travel` | RED, exit 101 | GREEN |
| Disable the Z-cut check | `waterjet_post_refuses_a_z_cut_and_a_cycle` | RED, exit 101 | GREEN |

Both red tests failed because the expected refusal was absent. The restored tests passed. The worktree is clean after restoration.

Requested before merge:

1. **Keep full-circle cuts when the post uses chords.** `crates/post/src/post/program_bounds.rs:101`. A valid radius-10 full-circle record starts and ends at `(10, 0)`. The circular option writes `G3 X10 Y0 I-10 J0 F300`. The linear option writes only `G1 X10 Y0 F300`, with no warning. The cut disappears. The existing `recorded/streams/full_circle_raw.cnc` uses equal endpoints. `segments3` treats equal endpoints as zero sweep. Split the circle before tessellation, or refuse it by name. Add tests for both directions.

2. **Reset the rapid cache when the work offset changes.** `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps:290`. I posted two sections with G54, then G55 and `OriginX=100`. The first section ends with `G0 X0 Y0`. The next section must rapid to absolute X100, which also formats as `X0 Y0` in G55. The cache removes that rapid. The output after G55 starts with the jet-on words, then `G1 X10 Y0`. It gives no warning. The jet opens at the old physical position. Clear the cache when the coordinate frame changes. Add a test with two work offsets.

3. **Carry the waterjet kind through the machine mirror.** `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps:148`. I supplied a valid vendor-tree machine with `general.kind: waterjet` and linear X/Y axes. The CLI parses it, then calls `machine::mirror`. The mirror drops the waterjet kind. This new check then reports `Review waterjet is not declared a waterjet machine` and writes no cut moves. Carry the kind through the mirror. Add a CLI test with a vendor-tree waterjet machine, rather than only the synthetic top-level `kind` object.

4. **Refuse a chord tolerance that the hard cap cannot meet.** `crates/post/src/post/program_bounds.rs:102`. A radius-1000 half circle with `chordTolerance=0.0001` produces 1,024 chords. I measured a maximum sagitta of `0.0011765482981900277` mm. This is more than eleven times the stated tolerance. The engine gives no warning. `segments3` silently caps the chord count. Check the required chord count or the resulting error. Meet the stated tolerance, or refuse the arc by name. Add a test that reaches the cap.

5. **Supply the required heavy-lane results.** `crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs:18` and the PR body, Tests. The changed CL source reaches every app and motion heavy target. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` selects 234 steps. The PR body names no heavy run. Current upstream rules require these results on the final head before the PR is ready. Run the reached heavy lanes after the fixes. State the head and results in the body. The dry run is not a pass.

Notes:

- The existing large files grow: `engine.rs` to 653 lines, `cnc.rs` to 1,074 lines, and `mod.rs` to 722 lines. This size note does not block the PR.
- The heavy lanes were planned but not run in this review. The PR needs changes regardless of the default-suite results.
- The isolated post inputs and NC outputs are under `/tmp`. No review evidence was committed or pushed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
